summary: A monthly report of ARPANET traffic for September 1973. It tabulates, for each Host, how many packets it sent, split between traffic that stayed within its own node and traffic sent to other nodes, with daily averages. It is a data memo and defines no protocol.

plainLanguage.summary: It is like a monthly count of how many cars used each road, written down so people can see which roads are busy.

questions: how much traffic did the arpanet carry in september 1973
how many packets did the arpanet carry in september 1973
why were arpanet traffic statistics removed from the rfc series
subtitle: BBN's table of how many packets each ARPANET host sent in September 1973, with a note that the reports may leave the RFC series.

tldr.problem: ARPANET sites wanted to know how much traffic each host was generating, and the author wondered whether monthly reports still belonged in the RFC series.
tldr.mechanism: BBN-NET attached a Host Throughput Summary for September 1973 and said he intends to issue October, November and December reports as RFCs and then stop.
tldr.outcome: The note asks readers to say if there is interest in continuing; RFC 586 later updated this report.

today: RFC 579 is a one-month data report, and RFC 586 updates it. It has no protocol content to be current or outdated.

sections.title: Cover Note
sections.content:
RFC 579, from A. McKenzie of BBN-NET, carries the traffic statistics for the month of September 1973. It updates RFC 566.

The note says he intends to issue Traffic Statistics for October, November and December in RFC form, and then to remove these reports from the RFC series. He will keep producing the reports and could have the NIC distribute them to technical Liaisons if there is interest, or continue issuing them as RFCs if there is great interest.
sections.plainLanguage: The person sending the scoreboard said he might stop posting it in this place unless people say they want it.

sections.title: How to Read the Table
sections.content:
The HOST THROUGHPUT SUMMARY (PACKETS OUTPUT) lists each host by site, with internode packets, intranode packets, a total, average daily internode packets and days counted (30 for September). Sites with several hosts get a subtotal.

ABER and LBL are listed as having had no traffic. This month's table also includes entries such as ULOND and TYMSH.
sections.plainLanguage: Every line is one computer and how many messages it sent, to far places and near ones.

sections.title: Network Totals
sections.content:
The network-wide totals are 86793910 internode packets and 22282380 intranode packets. The daily averages are 2893130 and 742746, and the average per node-day is 73804 and 18948.

PACKETS/MESSAGES (INTERNODE) is 1.07. Among the listed hosts, ISI HOST 1 had the most internode packets, 13157700.
sections.plainLanguage: At the bottom, all the numbers are added to show how busy the whole network was.

references.text: RFC 566, the earlier traffic statistics report that this RFC's header says it updates.
